title: Punjab after the Accord
body: In July 1985 Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal President Harchand Singh Longowal signed the Punjab Accord. Peace, however, did not come easily or immediately. The cycle of violence continued for nearly a decade. Militancy and counter-insurgency violence led to police excesses and violations of human rights, and the Akali Dal split into factions. The central government imposed President's rule in the State and normal electoral and political processes were suspended. When elections were finally held in 1992, only 24 per cent of the electors turned out to vote. Militancy was eventually eradicated by the security forces, and peace returned by the middle of the 1990s. In 1997, in the first normal elections of the post-militancy era, the alliance of the Akali Dal (Badal) and the BJP won a major victory.

title: The Assam Movement, 1979-1985
body: In 1979 the All Assam Students' Union, a students' group not linked to any party, led a movement against foreigners. Many Assamese suspected that there were huge numbers of illegal settlers from Bangladesh and feared that, unless these foreign nationals were detected and deported, the indigenous Assamese would be reduced to a minority. There were also economic issues. Despite natural resources like oil, tea and coal, Assam suffered widespread poverty and unemployment, and people felt these resources were drained out of the State without commensurate benefit to its people. The movement also opposed a faulty voters' register that included lakhs of immigrants. It used many novel methods, including trying to block trains and the supply of oil to refineries in Bihar, and drew support from all sections of Assamese society.
